column5: MBA attributes CRE debt to WHOEVER HOLDS THE NOTE, not to the ultimate investor. MBA methodology note, verbatim: 'many life insurance companies invest both in whole loans for which they hold the mortgage note (and which appear in this data under Life Insurance Companies) and in CMBS, CDOs and other ABS for which the security issuers and trustees hold the note (and which appear here under CMBS, CDO and other ABS issues).' column14: *** THE $775B IS A FLOOR ON INSURER CRE EXPOSURE, NOT A MEASURE OF IT. *** Real insurer CRE exposure = $775B PLUS an unpublished insurer share of the ~$637B securitized bucket. Consequence for the SHADE/PROME three-figure aggregate (Moody's $807B / Chicago Fed $849B / MBA $775B): the claim that the MBA figure is 'probably mostly distinct' from the other two is NOT a probability, it is a checkable yes/no -- do those perimeters include commercial mortgage WHOLE LOANS held at amortized cost? Those loans are a textbook illiquid non-market-marked insurer asset, i.e. exactly the defining property that aggregate uses, SO THE PRIOR SHOULD BE OVERLAP, NOT DISTINCTNESS. Strengthens the no-summing rule: the three perimeters are not merely unreconciled, they are DIFFERENTLY CONSTRUCTED -- MBA's is a note-holder attribution, so it is not even internally a measure of insurer exposure, and a figure that undercounts its own subject cannot be a summand. Also a 4th instance of SHADE's through-line 'the categories are set by the entities being measured' -- and the cleanest, because here NO ENTITY CHOSE: the measurement system splits one insurer's CRE risk across two buckets by the LEGAL FORM of the instrument rather than by who bears the loss. Routed to SHADE + PROME 2026-07-27; SHADE ADOPTED IN FULL and WITHDREW its 'probably mostly distinct' claim. *** SHADE'S COROLLARY, ROUTED BACK, AND IT LANDS ON CREED'S OWN FRAMING: the two MBA buckets are NOT 'securitized channel vs insurance channel' - they are 'note held by an insurer' vs 'note held by a trust'. AN INSURER BUYING A CMBS BOND PRINTS AS CMBS. So part of the -$9.6B 'CMBS shedding' may ITSELF be insurer-held, and the fast-sheds/slow-absorbs divergence may be an ARTIFACT OF INSTRUMENT LEGAL FORM rather than a migration between holder types. Stacked on the one-quarter problem (Q4-2025 CMBS/CDO/ABS was +$3.6B POSITIVE), that is TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS not to carry FLOW-CREED-08 as an established mechanism. And note: even two consecutive quarters in opposite directions would NOT settle the legal-form question - it is not a sample-size problem. FLOW-CREED-08 stands as real-but-UNESTABLISHED. ***

The three "3.40" strings are unrelated table cells (an equity-capital-ratio series, a regional table, a time series); the one "3.4 percent" is UNREALIZED LOSSES ON HTM SECURITIES. *** AND THE EDITION HAS ONLY EIGHT CHARTS -- THERE IS NO CHART 11. *** The chart carrying the series is a Q4-2025 feature, absent from Q1-2026 entirely, so this is not a text-extraction limitation: the series is not in that edition in ANY shape. || *** CONFIRMED AT A SECOND CONSECUTIVE EDITION 2026-08-28 -- n=2, AND THE Q2 QBP DOES NOT CLARIFY THE SERIES QUESTION. *** FDIC Q2-2026 QBP PRIMARY-READ on a FRESH own download 2026-08-28 (fdic.gov/quarterly-banking-profile/quarterly-banking-profile-second-quarter-2026.pdf, 1,012,102 bytes, 27 pages, 188,564 chars, pdfminer).
